'''Dan Wesley Urry''' (September 14, 1935 – November 30, 2020) was an American biophysicist and chemist known for his work in the field of [[molecular biophysics]], particularly in the study of [[bioelastic materials]] and [[protein-based polymers]].  Urry published over 490 scientific papers, held 28 US patents, and was a well cited scientist in the 1980s.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Dr. Dan W. Urry Obituary 2020 |url=https://www.curriejefferson.com/obituaries/drdanw-urry |access-date=2024-10-20 |website=Currie-Jefferson Funeral Home & Memorial Gardens |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":1" />

== Early life and education ==
Urry earned his BA degree in [[medical biology]] in 1960 from the University of Utah, where he graduated with high honors. He continued his studies at the University of Utah, obtaining a PhD in physical chemistry in 1964 under the mentorship of [[Henry Eyring (chemist)|Henry Eyring]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Collection: Dan Wesley Urry papers {{!}} ArchivesSpace Public Interface |url=https://archivespace.lib.utah.edu/repositories/3/resources/3098 |access-date=2024-10-20 |website=archivespace.lib.utah.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Mortensen |first1=Earl M. |last2=Eyring |first2=Henry |date= 1960|title=Transmission Coefficients for Evaporation and Condensation |url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/j100836a004 |journal=The Journal of Physical Chemistry |language=en |volume=64 |issue=7 |pages=846–849 |doi=10.1021/j100836a004 |issn=0022-3654|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== Academic and research career ==
He began as a fellow at [[Harvard University]] and the [[University of California, Berkeley]], before joining the Institute of Biomedical Research of The American Medical Association in 1965. He became a tenured full member in 1969 and concurrently held a position as professorial lecturer at the [[University of Chicago]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Faculty < Wesleyan University |url=https://catalog.wesleyan.edu/faculty/ |access-date=2024-10-20 |website=catalog.wesleyan.edu}}</ref><ref name=":0" />

At the University of Alabama at Birmingham he served from 1970 to 1997 as professor of biochemistry and the director of the Laboratory of [[Molecular Biophysics]], with additional appointments in physiology, biophysics, and adjunct professor of physics.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Urry, Dan Wesley |url=https://archivespace.lib.utah.edu/agents/people/3475 |website=archivespace.lib.utah.edu}}</ref>

From 1997 to 2008, Urry continued his academic career at the University of Minnesota-Twin Cities, where he was a professor of chemical engineering and [[materials science]], and later Professor of Biophysics.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Dan W Urry |url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Dan-Urry |website=researchgate.net}}</ref>

== Personal life and legacy ==
Urry was married to Kathleen Lake, with whom he had one child. And was previously married in which he had three boys.
